# ADR-042 · `CHANGELOG.md` is only regenerated by hand via `make docs`; it never enters a commit without review (2026-10-27, Angel)

**Context.** The `Makefile` separates `check` (depends on `docs-check`, no `git-cliff`) from `docs` (which runs `git-cliff -o CHANGELOG.md`). During T-06b, `make docs` ran and a subsequent `git add -A` swept the freshly generated `CHANGELOG.md` into a commit Angel never reviewed. It wasn't false content, just unreviewed.
**Options.** (a) rely on discipline (`revision-pre-commit` already asks to review `git diff --cached`, but that wasn't enough); (b) take `git-cliff` out of `make docs` into a separate command; (c) `.gitignore` it so it's never tracked unless Angel adds it by hand after reviewing.
**Decision.** (c). `CHANGELOG.md` is removed from the offending commit (amended locally, not pushed) and added to `.gitignore`. `make docs` still regenerates it on disk (Angel needs to see it), but git ignores it by default: it only enters a commit via `git add -f CHANGELOG.md` after review.
**Why.** `.gitignore` is the only option that makes the omission automatic instead of relying on someone remembering to check the diff every time.
**What would invalidate it.** The repo needing a continuously versioned CHANGELOG.md (e.g. for the public README) → re-track it and make review an explicit step in `revision-pre-commit`.
